::: {.lead}
Fourteen practical articles. One small Go notebook service. Start with your first request and finish with a framework you can explain.
:::

## What you will build

Pocket Notes accepts a title, saves it in memory, and returns a list of notes. Along the way, you will build routing, JSON helpers, validation, middleware, cancellation, storage interfaces, and tests.

::: {.callout-note}
The core examples require Go 1.22+ and use only the standard library. Database, cache, and account features are clearly marked as extension designs. Notes in the supplied application disappear after restart.
:::

## First connections

- [00 · A small project, a clear destination](en/00-start.qmd) — Set up your desk, learn just enough Go, and decide what we are building.
- [01 · Follow one request all the way home](en/01-request.qmd) — Understand the conversation before adding abstractions.
- [02 · Give each action an address](en/02-routing.qmd) — Design the notebook API and wrap the router in a tiny engine.
- [03 · Make responses boring and consistent](en/03-response.qmd) — Build a request wrapper and a small JSON helper.

## A useful core

- [04 · Treat input as a question, not a fact](en/04-input.qmd) — Accept one small JSON object and reject mistakes clearly.
- [05 · Wrap a handler without changing its job](en/05-middleware.qmd) — Use middleware for request timing and learn why order matters.
- [06 · Stop work nobody needs anymore](en/06-cancellation.qmd) — Use cooperative cancellation without racing the response writer.
- [07 · Give your data a home](en/07-storage.qmd) — Separate note storage from HTTP and handle concurrent requests.

## Make it dependable

- [08 · Turn expectations into tests](en/08-tests.qmd) — Check the API without opening a port or clicking a browser.
- [09 · Start clearly. Stop cleanly.](en/09-lifecycle.qmd) — Make configuration, logs, and shutdown part of the application.
- [10 · Keep data after the process exits](en/10-persistence.qmd) — Plan a database adapter, then decide whether a cache is worth adding.
- [11 · Make the easy path repeatable](en/11-workflow.qmd) — Organize files, document the API, and automate a few useful steps.

## Put it together

- [12 · Connect a browser, then draw the trust boundary](en/12-browser.qmd) — Render notes safely and understand what adding accounts really requires.
- [13 · Ship a small thing you understand](en/13-finish.qmd) — Run the complete project, inspect its boundaries, and plan the next iteration.
